set.body:
Objective:
Add high-value pure logical normalization and capability-driven, resource-safe source/sink boundaries without building a production physical optimizer or allowing backends to redefine Frame semantics.

Logical normalization scope:
- Projection pruning through filters, aggregates, joins, sorts, and nested projections.
- Predicate composition and source pushdown only where SourceCapabilities prove support.
- Null- and floating-aware expression simplification.
- Filter/projection fusion, limit pushdown, and redundant projection elimination.
- Every rewrite is explainable and tested for semantic equivalence by executing original and normalized plans over generated batches.

Boundary with production engines:
- Core owns lawful logical rewrites and residual-plan accounting.
- A backend owns physical planning only after declaring capabilities; pure plan.explain does not pretend to know backend costs or copies.
- Backend explain reports requested, accepted, and residual pushdown plus buffering, allocation, and copy receipts.

Source and sink protocol:
- Sources expose schema inspection separately from lazy data scanning.
- Scan requests carry column selection, portable predicate, limit, and batch-size hints.
- Capabilities describe projection, predicate, limit, partition, statistics, and streaming support.
- Plans hold immutable source descriptions; FS2 execution scopes opening, scanning, cancellation, early termination, and closing readers.
- Sinks consume batch streams and return structured receipts.

Baseline foundation adapters:
- In-memory record batches.
- CSV with explicit inference/coercion policy.
- Arrow IPC where a conforming platform adapter exists, with shared fixtures establishing equivalent schemas and values.
- Parquet and production query engines remain separate adapter motes and are not foundation release requirements.

Acceptance:
- Normalization-equivalence laws cover nulls, NaNs, chunks, aliases, and join/aggregate dependencies.
- A pushed-down scan reads only required columns and demonstrates early termination when supported.
- Unsupported pushdown remains above the source rather than disappearing.
- Schema inspection, source, sink, cancellation, allocation, and close failures are structured ADTs.
- Pure logical explain and backend physical explain are both deterministic and clearly distinguished.
set.title: Frame foundation 5: lawful normalization and capability-driven FS2 sources, sinks, CSV, and Arrow IPC
